Bug_Title: Map values should not be replaced unconditionally
Bug_Details:
Storing a value inside a collection at a given key or index and then unconditionally overwriting it without reading the initial value is a case of
a "dead store".
letters.put("a", "Apple");
letters.put("a", "Boy");  // Noncompliant

towns[i] = "London";
towns[i] = "Chicago";  // Noncompliant
This practice is redundant and will cause confusion for the reader. More importantly, it is often an error and not what the developer intended to
do.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the line letters.put("a", "Boy"); which replaces the value for the key "a" without checking its original value.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by adding a duplicate key to the map and then checking the value associated with that key.
